C000.why: Adds a substantive condition ('resulting in continuous acceleration') to the misapplication trigger definition, changing what the system must detect.

C001.why: Extends the ACPE obligation from standstill only to also cover creeping.

C002.why: Major change to the core performance requirement: new distance range, new obstacle types and new boundary conditions.

C003.why: Test lateral offset tolerance widened from 0.2 m to the vehicle edge, a substantive test change.

C004.why: Test now defined by the trigger distance rather than the start position; substantive, though phrased as a Technical Service action.

C005.why: Mostly editorial; only the word 'relevant' was added.

C006.why: Removes a manufacturer-requested pre-test allowance; this is a test-procedure allowance, so moderate likelihood.

C007.why: New exemption conditions (AEBS active, speed above 10 km/h) that change the ACPE obligation.

C008.why: New performance requirement for collisions while creeping.

C009.why: Describes what the technical service must ensure during testing.

C011.why: Defines the vehicle reference point; close to a definition, but part of the test setup.

C012.why: New test condition for the pedestrian lateral offset.

C014.why: Vehicle target orientation with technical service choice; a test parameter.

C015.why: Tests with and without the target are now an explicit requirement for a stationary vehicle.

C018.why: New creeping test procedure, but at technical service discretion.

C019.why: New creeping test condition targeting the forward creeping speed.

C020.why: New creeping test condition targeting 4 km/h in the rearward direction.

C021.why: Test procedure step for creeping tests.

C022.why: Test procedure step for creeping tests.

C023.why: Test procedure step for creeping tests.

C024.why: Test procedure step linking the trigger to the Table 1 distance.

C025.why: This is a new test-procedure provision tied to a performance requirement (5.1.6.2) for cases where a collision is not prevented. However, it is phrased as a duty to demonstrate to the technical service, which experts often treat as evidence submission. It sits within a newly added test section, so it is likely relevant but borderline.
